weakness: The program released the bowl over the middle of the basin without looking at what was already in it. With a pot standing there the bowl came to rest on top of the pot, above the sink's rim. The first repair then picked a free spot the arm could not reach at carry height and, when the carry stopped, released the bowl on the counter.
how_found: I questioned A1 (the basin is empty): the release point and release height were computed from the sink's box alone, and real sinks usually hold dishes or a pot.
why_missed: Every Phase-1 scene had an empty sink, so treating the container's interior as free space never failed; the destination was computed from the container's geometry instead of from what occupies it.
fix: List the things standing inside the basin (averaged obstacle boxes overlapping it, taller than its floor); rank release points by the room left around the bowl's whole footprint, then by nearness to the robot; carry the bowl above the tallest of them; if the arm cannot reach a spot, try the next; release only after re-detecting the bowl over the basin.
general_rule: Before putting an object into a container, look at what already occupies it and choose a spot with room for the object's whole footprint that the arm can actually reach; never release until the object is verified over that spot.

weakness: The program chose the arm from the side of the robot the bowl was on and assumed that arm could also carry it to the sink. With the bowl on the far side of the counter, the left arm picked it up, could reach none of the release spots, and the program stopped with the bowl in its hand.
how_found: I questioned A10 (the bowl is within reach of the arm that carries it): the arm choice looked only at where the bowl was, not at where it had to go.
why_missed: In every Phase-1 scene the bowl spawned on the sink's side of the counter, so one arm could always do the whole job; reach was never tested between the pick and the place.
fix: If the arm holding the bowl reaches no release spot, set the bowl down on a free counter spot between the arms (both reach it), send that arm home, pick the bowl up with the other arm and deliver it.
general_rule: Check that the arm that picks an object can also reach where it must go; when no single arm can do both, hand the object over through a free intermediate spot both arms reach instead of giving up.

weakness: The program chose its release spot once, before the carry, and let go there without looking again; a pot shoved into that spot during the carry caught the bowl on top of it. Once it did look again, the only free part of the basin was its far half, which a hand pointing straight down cannot reach at any height.
how_found: I questioned A11 (nothing about the sink changes during the episode): the free-spot choice from round 1 was a single snapshot taken seconds before the release.
why_missed: Every earlier scene was static, so a decision made at the start was still true at the end; and every spot chosen so far lay in the near half of the basin, so the hand never needed another orientation.
fix: Just before lowering, wait until whatever is in the basin is still (two averaged looks 0.5 s apart agree), re-check that the spot still has room for the whole footprint, and choose again if not; to reach a far spot, pitch the hand towards it (0.5 or 0.9 rad; the bowl tilts with the hand and is carried higher by the drop of its low edge) or turn the hand so the bowl hangs on the far side; as a last resort accept a spot where only the bowl's centre is over free floor.
general_rule: Re-observe the destination immediately before an irreversible action, after letting moving things settle, and re-plan if it changed, including the hand orientation needed to reach the new choice.
